'''Jonathan P. Dowling''' (3 April 1955 – 5 June 2020) was an Irish-American researcher and professor in theoretical physics, known for his work on [[quantum technology]], particularly for exploiting [[quantum entanglement]] (in the form of a [[NOON state]]) for applications to [[quantum metrology]], [[quantum sensing]], and [[quantum imaging]].

==Career==
Dowling obtained a PhD in 1988 from the University of Colorado-Boulder.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|author=Louisiana State University (LSU) |url=https://www.lsu.edu/physics/people/faculty/dowling.php |title=Jonathan Dowling |publisher=Lsu.edu |date= |access-date=2020-06-07}}</ref> He worked at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]],<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.41.2284|title = Self-field quantum electrodynamics: The two-level atom|year = 1990|last1 = Barut|first1 = A. O.|last2 = Dowling|first2 = Jonathan P.|journal = Physical Review A|volume = 41|issue = 5|pages = 2284–2294|pmid = 9903354|bibcode = 1990PhRvA..41.2284B}}</ref> the [[United States Army Aviation and Missile Command]],<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1063/1.356336|title = The photonic band edge laser: A new approach to gain enhancement|year = 1994|last1 = Dowling|first1 = Jonathan P.|last2 = Scalora|first2 = Michael|last3 = Bloemer|first3 = Mark J.|last4 = Bowden|first4 = Charles M.|journal = Journal of Applied Physics|volume = 75|issue = 4|pages = 1896–1899|bibcode = 1994JAP....75.1896D}}</ref> the NASA [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://trs.jpl.nasa.gov/bitstream/handle/2014/18711/99-2095.pdf |title=Info |publisher=trs.jpl.nasa.gov/bitstream |date= |access-date=2020-06-07}}</ref> and the [[Louisiana State University]].<ref name=":0" />

Dowling was one of the founders of the US Government program in quantum computing and [[quantum cryptography]].<ref>"Quantum computing and communications," by Michael Brooks (London, Springer, 1999), page 107, Quote from this book: "Although this is not widely known, the American NSA-ARO-DARPA research programme in quantum computing was kindled, indirectly, by European speakers and communicated to the US funding agencies by ''Jon Dowling'' who was, at the time, a physicist in the U.S. Army Aviation and Missile Command.... Jon had attended the 1994 IQEC and ICAP meeting where British Telecom revealed their transmission of a quantum cryptographic key over 10km of optical fiber, and Artur Ekert announced Shor's discovery of the factoring algorithm, respectively. Upon making these breakthroughs known to the Army Research Office, it was decided to have an ARO workshop on quantum cryptography and quantum computing in Tucson in the winter of 1995. Many of the key researchers in quantum computing were at this workshop, as well as Keith Miller and others from the National Security Agency (NSA). This workshop was the genesis of the ARO-NSA collaboration on the promotion of quantum computing research." http://www.worldcat.org/oclc/901463471</ref>

Dowling was the co-director of the [[Horace Hearne Institute|Horace Hearne Institute for Theoretical Physics]] and a Hearne chair in theoretical physics at the department of physics and astronomy, both at [[Louisiana State University]].

==Research==
Dowling authored scientific publications in [[quantum electrodynamics]], [[quantum optics]], and [[quantum technology]]. At the time of his death, his publications had been cited over 20,200 times, with a [[Hirsch index]] of 64.<ref>Dowling's Google Scitations https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=3YObZBIAAAAJ&hl=en</ref> 

Dowling published papers are on the topics of [[Linear optical quantum computing]],<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.79.135| title=Linear optical quantum computing with photonic qubits| year=2007| last1=Kok| first1=Pieter| last2=Munro| first2=W. ==Publications==
Dowling is the author of a [[popular science]] book, "Schrödinger's Killer App – Race to Build the World's First Quantum Computer".<ref>{{Cite book|title=Schrödinger's killer app: race to build the world's first quantum computer|last=P.|first=Dowling, Jonathan|date = 7 May 2013|isbn=9781439896730|location=Boca Raton|oclc=746838207}}</ref> A story in this book about early motivations for funding [[quantum computing]] by the United States military was illustrated by [[Saturday Morning Breakfast Cereal]] following his death.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Saturday Morning Breakfast Cereal - Jonathan Dowling|url=https://www.smbc-comics.com/comic/jonathan-dowling|access-date=2020-07-03|website=www.smbc-comics.com}}</ref> Additionally, this book formulated what is known as the Dowling-Neven Law,<ref name="dowling-memorial-nat-phot">{{cite journal |last1=Franson |first1=James |last2=Wilde |first2=Mark |title=Jonathan Patrick Dowling in memoriam |journal=Nature Photonics |date=August 12, 2020 |volume=14 |issue=9 |pages=525–526 |doi=10.1038/s41566-020-0682-1 |bibcode=2020NaPho..14..525F |s2cid=225489566 |access-date=2023-01-08|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41566-020-0682-1|hdl=11603/19954 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> regarding the classical cost of simulating quantum computers growing doubly exponentially in time, given that the number of qubits on current quantum computers is currently growing exponentially with time. The first book's sequel, "Schrödinger's Web: Race to Build the Quantum Internet", has been released posthumously.<ref>{{Cite book|date=2020|title=Taylor & Francis Group: Schrödinger's Web: Race to Build the Quantum Internet|doi=10.1201/9780367337629|url=https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/9780367337629|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|last1=Dowling|first1=Jonathan P.|isbn=978-0-367-33762-9}}</ref> 

Dowling co-authored a 2003 paper which predicted a boom in quantum technologies.<ref>"Quantum technology: the second quantum revolution," by 
Jonathan P. Dowling & Gerard J. Milburn; Published 15 August 2003; DOI:10.1098/rsta.2003.1227 [http://www.phys.lsu.edu/~jdowling/publications/Dowling03.pdf]</ref>
